sample_unit: participants (adults with MRI scans under no, low, and high motion conditions)

links.outcome: Brain age estimate reliability and error under varying MRI head-motion conditions across five algorithms
links.effect: Motion significantly impacted estimates for some algorithms; ICCs dropped as low as 0.609 and errors rose up to 11.5 years for high motion scans. DeepBrainNet and pyment were most robust (ICCs 0.956-0.965).
links.quote: Results demonstrated motion significantly impacted brain age estimates for some algorithms, with ICCs dropping as low as 0.609 and errors increasing up to 11.5 years for high motion scans.

links.outcome: Comparative reliability and robustness of five brain age algorithms on the same motion-varied MRI data
links.effect: DeepBrainNet and pyment showed greatest robustness (ICCs 0.956-0.965); XGBoost and brainageR had largest errors (up to 13.5 RMSE) and bias with motion.
links.quote: DeepBrainNet and pyment showed greatest robustness and reliability (ICCs = 0.956-0.965).

screen.reason: Evaluates the robustness/reliability of existing brain age algorithms against MRI motion artifacts on retrospective datasets without testing a deployment safeguard or workflow intervention.
